Article Title: Second Vande Bharat sleeper set to launch this month between Bengaluru and Mumbai; cutting travel time from 24 hours to under 16 hours, 30 year wait for faster connectivity between two cities to end
Article Text:
For more than 30 years, passengers have been seeking faster rail connectivity between Bengaluru and Mumbai.

Mumbai-Bengaluru Vande Bharat Sleeper: Expected Travel Time

What makes Vande Bharat sleeper special?

Vande Bharat sleeper: Indian Railways is all set to roll out the second Vande Bharat sleeper train after launching the first pair between Guwahati and Howrah earlier this year.After prolonged delays, the Railway Board is expected to issue the notification for the KSR Bengaluru-Mumbai CSMT Vande Bharat Sleeper shortly. According to sources, the train is likely to be flagged off later this month.The country's second Vande Bharat sleeper service is expected to substantially reduce the time taken to travel by rail between Bengaluru, India's technology hub, and Mumbai, its financial capital.Also Read | With better than Rajdhani experience & 160 kmph speed, can Vande Bharat sleeper trains be a game-changer for Indian Railways? Under the proposed schedule, the premium train will run six days a week in each direction, covering the distance in under 16 hours. At present, the Udyan Express, the only direct daily train connecting the two cities, takes an average of 24 hours to complete the journey.As per the tentative timings, the service may leave KSR Bengaluru at 10 PM and arrive at Mumbai CSMT at 1:50 PM the next day. On the return journey, it could start from Mumbai at 10:30 PM, reaching Bengaluru at 1:50 PM the following day. These are tentative timings and are subject to change.Although the official launch date has not yet been declared, the railway zones have been asked to commence the service at the earliest convenient opportunity.Its scheduled halts will include Anantapur, Guntakal, Raichur, Kalaburagi, Solapur and Kalyan, according to this TOI report For more than 30 years, passengers have been seeking faster rail connectivity between Bengaluru and Mumbai. Despite repeated assurances, train journeys between the two cities continue to take considerable time.The proposed Vande Bharat Sleeper service is expected to address this long-standing demand and improve connectivity between the cities.The Vande Bharat sleeper train has 16 passenger coaches. The rake includes 11 AC 3-tier coaches, four AC 2-tier coaches and one AC First Class coach.The train has been designed to operate at speeds of up to 160 kmph, while its testing speed is 180 kmph, placing it in the semi-high-speed category. However, most sections of the Indian Railways network are not equipped to permit trains to operate at such high speeds.Drawing on design elements seen in European trains, the Vande Bharat sleeper coaches feature cushioned berths aimed at providing greater comfort. The design of the upper berths has also been modified to make climbing up easier for passengers.Passenger amenities include dedicated night lights, integrated public announcement systems accompanied by visual displays, CCTV cameras and modular pantry units.The sleeper train is also equipped with modern bio-vacuum toilets similar to those used in aircraft. A separate toilet designed for disabled passengers also has a baby care station. Passengers travelling in AC First Class additionally have access to shower facilities with hot water.For safety, the Vande Bharat sleeper train comes fitted with the indigenous KAVACH anti-collision system. Like the chair car versions of Vande Bharat, the sleeper variant will also use regenerative braking technology to improve energy efficiency.Automatic interconnecting doors have been provided between the coaches. The gangways are fully sealed, helping maintain clean air inside the train as well as effective temperature control.Passenger convenience features in every coach include individual reading lights, charging points and refreshment tables. The interiors use GFRP panels. The train doors are designed to open automatically at designated stations.The train also comes with a Centralised Coach Monitoring System. An emergency communication facility allows passengers to communicate directly with the driver when required.Meanwhile, ICF is also working on developing its own version of the Vande Bharat sleeper train.
Article Summary: The KSR Bengaluru-Mumbai CSMT Vande Bharat Sleeper is likely to be flagged off later this month. The premium train will run six days a week in each direction, covering the distance in under 16 hours. At present, the Udyan Express, the only direct daily train connecting the two cities, takes an average of 24 hours.

Article Title: Apple is making changes to its OS for Macs after users' complain about Meta's AI Agent Muse accessing their 'private data'
Article Text:
Apple's complete statement on updates to Full Disk Access in macOS

Apple is planning to change its Mac operating system, and the reason are AI Agents. The company wants to make it more clear to users when AI agents ask ​to access all of the data on their Macs. The announcement comes after some users have criticized Meta's ‌Muse, an AI agent for accessing their private messages. While on ​Apple's iPhones and iPads, no single app can access data inside another ​app by default, company's Macs are ⁠more flexible. Apple Macs come with a 'Full Disk Access' option that allows apps such as cloud ​backup services to access all the data on a machine, with a user's permission.In an update posted on its developer website, Apple said that some developers were using the Full Disk Access feature in ways that could put users at risk. "Going forward, we will introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely ​wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so ​with very explicit user action," Apple wrote."As AI agents become increasingly capable and autonomous, ‌the ⁠risks associated with this level of access will grow substantially. We are committed to ensuring users clearly understand these risks before granting such access, so they can make informed decisions about their own data and privacy."Apple's announcement comes after a technology ​columnist in Inc magazine accused ​Meta's Muse of ⁠reading private messages on his Mac. "In fact, I remember explicitly choosing not to let it have access to my messages, calendar, and other personal information," he wrote. He claimed that he had not enabled Full Disk Access and further added that when he asked Muse to explain how this occurred, the AI said that it was syncing his "device notifications. " Similarly, a YouTuber named Matt Robb recently said that Muse mishandled a task in which he was selling things on Facebook Marketplace, leading to his address being shared.Meta spokesperson Andy Stone disputed the claims saying that Muse's access to Apple's Messages app ​is strictly ⁠opt-in. "You have to enable both Full Disk Access and the Messages connector for Muse to be able to read your Messages content," Stone wrote on social media platform X, opens new tab. "It ⁠can't read ​your Messages unless you do this. And it ​can be revoked at any time.""We give developers powerful APIs to build incredible capabilities into their apps for Apple products, backed by a set of controls designed to protect users’ private data. Full Disk Access largely sidesteps these controls in order to allow backup apps to function properly on the Mac. Some developers are using Full Disk Access in ways that could put users at risk, exposing everything on their systems -- including files, mail, messages, and even browsing history -- without users’ full knowledge and understanding. For communication apps, this can also compromise the privacy of the people users are communicating with.""Going forward, we will introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action. Addressing this is critical. As AI agents become increasingly capable and autonomous, the risks associated with this level of access will grow substantially. We are committed to ensuring users clearly understand these risks before granting such access, so they can make informed decisions about their own data and privacy. "
Article Summary: Apple is planning to change its Mac operating system, and the reason are AI Agents. The company wants to make it more clear to users when AI agents ask ​to access all of the data on their Macs. The announcement comes after some users have criticized Meta's ‌Muse, an AI agent for accessing their private messages.

Article Title: Meta lets go co-founders and employees of AI startup Virtue AI, four months after the company hired them; Andy Stone admits differences over style of working
Article Text:
Meta lets go co-founders and employees of AI startup Virtue AI, four months after the company hired them; Andy Stone admits differences over style of working

Meta says Virtue AI arrangement did not work out

Meta hired Virtue AI founders in June

Why Meta hired the Virtue AI team

Meta continues AI safety push

Meta has made similar AI team hires

Meta is letting go of employees from an AI security startup it acquired just months ago. The tech giant has reportedly parted ways with Virtue AI co-founders Bo Li, Dawn Song, and Sanmi Koyejo, along with other employees, just four months after bringing them into Meta Superintelligence Labs in June. Meta spokesperson Andy Stone confirmed the departures to Semafor and said the arrangement did not work out as planned because of differences in working styles.The move comes after Meta had recruited the Virtue AI team to strengthen its efforts around AI safety, security and frontier risks. The startup had previously worked with companies including Anthropic and OpenAI, as well as the Commerce Department’s National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST).Meta spokesperson Andy Stone confirmed the departures to Semafor and attributed the decision to differences in how the team worked.“Unfortunately, the arrangement didn’t work out as planned,” Stone said, adding that Meta Superintelligence Labs remains focused on AI safety, alignment and frontier risk.The departures come as Meta continues to shape its AI strategy and expand its capabilities around increasingly advanced AI systems.The company has been investing heavily in artificial intelligence, while AI safety and security have also become a growing focus for technology companies and policymakers.In June, Axios reported that Meta Superintelligence Labs hired Virtue AI co-founders Bo Li, Dawn Song and Sanmi Koyejo, along with other members of the startup’s team.The hiring aimed to strengthen Meta’s security efforts around AI agents at a time when concerns about the safety of increasingly capable AI systems were growing.Virtue AI had developed enterprise AI security tools covering automated red teaming, runtime guardrails and AI governance. The startup had also previously worked with Anthropic, OpenAI and the Commerce Department’s NIST. However, the terms of the arrangement were not disclosed.“As we ship AI products to billions of people and build increasingly capable agents, keeping those systems safe, reliable, and trustworthy is foundational,” the memo says.Li and Song were set to report to Nat Friedman, a Meta Superintelligence Labs executive, while Koyejo was expected to report to Rob Fergus, head of Meta's fundamental AI research lab, FAIR.Meta's decision to bring in the Virtue AI founders reflected the company's broader push to strengthen AI security as it develops more capable models and agents.The startup's work focused on identifying potential risks in AI systems and developing tools to test and safeguard them. Its technology included automated red teaming to identify weaknesses in AI systems, as well as runtime guardrails and governance tools.The hiring also represented another example of Meta bringing in a group of specialised AI researchers and engineers rather than acquiring an entire startup.Despite the departure of the Virtue AI team, Stone said Meta Superintelligence Labs remains focused on AI safety, alignment and frontier risk.The development comes as AI companies face increasing scrutiny over how they develop, test and deploy increasingly capable systems. AI agents, in particular, have become a growing area of focus as companies work on systems that can perform more complex tasks with less human intervention.Meta's decision to recruit the Virtue AI team in June was part of that broader push. However, the arrangement lasted only four months before the company decided to let the employees go.The Virtue AI hiring was also part of Meta's broader strategy to recruit specialised teams from smaller AI companies.Meta poached the founders and team behind Dreamer, an AI startup focused on helping people build agents, in March. The approach allows the company to bring in specialised talent and expertise without necessarily acquiring an entire company.The Virtue AI departures now mark a much shorter-lived version of that strategy, with Meta confirming that differences in working styles contributed to the arrangement ending.The company, however, continues to expand its AI operations as the race to develop increasingly capable models and agents intensifies.
Article Summary: Virtue AI co-founders Bo Li, Dawn Song, and Sanmi Koyejo have been let go by Meta Superintelligence Labs. The tech giant hired the Virtue AI team in June to strengthen its efforts around AI safety, security and frontier risks. The departures come as Meta continues to shape its AI strategy.

Article Title: Apple may unveil new smart home hub, HomePod mini and Apple TV on October 13: Report
Article Text:
Apple may unveil new smart home hub, HomePod mini and Apple TV on October 13: Report

Apple’s new smart home hub could get a screen

HomePod mini may get S11 chip

New Apple TV could focus on performance

Apple is planning to hold an event on October 13, 2026, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman said in the latest edition of his weekly PowerOn newsletter. At the event, the company is expected to unveil its “long-awaited smart home hub with a screen, the new HomePod mini and an updated Apple TV,” Gurman stated. All three devices will have Siri AI at the core, he added. This will be the company’s first event after the September event where it unveiled 2026 iPhone lineup – iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, along with iPhone Duo. Apple’s October 13 event could mark a major push into smart home devices. Here’s what to expectThe most notable launch is expected to be a new smart home hub with a built-in display, which could compete with devices such as Google Nest Hub and Amazon Echo Show. The device is rumoured to feature an S11 chip, which could support faster performance and Siri AI features. The screen could be used to show information such as weather updates, calendar events and music controls.A FaceTime camera is also among the expected features, potentially allowing the device to double as a video-calling hub. Apple is also reportedly developing a specialised operating system for the device focused on smart home controls.Apple is also expected to introduce an updated HomePod mini. The overall design may remain largely unchanged, while an upgraded S11 chip could improve performance and Siri responsiveness. The speaker could also get tighter integration with Apple’s smart home ecosystem and potentially new colour options.The third expected launch is an updated Apple TV. The device is rumoured to receive a more powerful chip, potentially the A19 or A19 Pro, which could improve gaming, streaming and multitasking. The updated Apple TV could also feature deeper Siri AI integration for voice-controlled navigation and smart home functions. Other possible additions include HDMI pass-through and a redesigned Siri Remote.All three devices are expected to have Siri AI at the core, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, making the October event potentially important for Apple’s wider smart home strategy.

Article Title: ‘AI disrupts, but offers avenues to take on large incumbents’
Article Text:
Murali Swaminathan, chief technology officer of Freshworks

Murali Swaminathan

How is AI changing SaaS?

What changed the way you build software as you target upmarket customers?

How can companies like Freshworks differentiate?

As SaaS companies move towards automating workflows, what security measures are required?

How are you adopting agentic AI?

What is your advice for freshers?

How should they approach education?





AI is disrupting software building and creating competitive pressures, while creating new opportunities for SaaS (Software as a Service) companies, says, chief technology officer of Freshworks. The company is adapting to this shift, changing how it designs, engineers and develops products. In an interview, he discusses how agentic AI is deployed in large enterprises and how youngsters entering the job market should approach skilling. Excerpts:AI is no longer altering how people use software, it is changing how software is built and how work gets done. AI makes building easier and faster. Now that everyone can be a builder, there is increasing competitive pressure and we are getting disrupted. But that is a positive, as we are learning and transforming. Competitors make us stronger, and we are now able to compete with big players serving large enterprise customers. Freshworks is adapting its internal product development processes and changing how our teams think and build.Core engineering fundamentals do not change, but enterprise expectations and business approaches are different.Massive enterprise deals demand higher system resiliency and urgent support. The go-to-market motion (how we sell and deliver the product) shifts from anonymous, self-serve usage to a lengthy, high-touch relationship. This requires sharing our future roadmaps in advance, offering complete transparency, engaging directly with executives, and providing hands-on trials.While AI makes building initial software prototypes fast and effortless, the challenges remain- scaling applications, ensuring system resilience and maintaining consistent operations across thousands of enterprise users. So, the conversation has shifted from merely experimenting with AI to operationalising it safely and reliably at a massive scale. Technology is rapidly advancing beyond basic chat assistants toward networks of agents and fully autonomous systems. It is a decade-long journey with vast opportunities as AI-driven software transforms how complex work gets done. We are moving from simple AI copilots that just assist users, to AI agents that can execute multi-step tasks, invoke tools and take real actions.I see enterprise software evolving into a trusted system of record, context and control. As AI agents move from just answering questions to taking actions, safety guardrails cannot live only inside the AI model itself. An enterprise agent needs an identity, defined permissions, and a clear scope of authority much like a human worker does. An agent summarizing a document is different from one changing critical production infrastructure or modifying system access. As the potential business impact increases, so should verification and oversight. This is where mature SaaS platforms remain vital. They provide systems of record, APIs, workflows, role-based access, and audit trails. Even if users increasingly interact through AI agents instead of traditional screens, these agents still need that trusted foundation. The real advantage is combining trusted context, identity, permissions, and controls.A lot of emphasis on adopting AI agents in enterprises focuses on governance and security, which includes giving these agents role-based access similar to human workers. We are introducing an entity called a non-human agent or “digital worker”, AI agents acting on an employee’s behalf. These digital workers are treated as personal identities with scoped, time-bound permissions. For example, an employee could temporarily delegate authority to their digital worker while on vacation. To maintain enterprise governance and accountability, system logs must explicitly distinguish between actions performed directly by a human and those executed by their digital worker.AI is only as good as the person using it. As basic coding tasks are increasingly automated, entry-level expectations are higher now. Youngsters must use AI to delegate routine work so they can focus on solving more complex problems. Crucially, they must understand core computer science and programming fundamentals to judge whether AI-generated code is correct and challenge it when necessary.While catching the AI wave early is valuable, completing a college degree remains essential. It provides structured learning, human experience, networking, and a broad foundation that self-taught building alone cannot replace. Candidates are expected to present a portfolio of things they built, a simple app for the family, a cloud deployment, or a small tool. Employers expect candidates to know basic platforms.
Article Summary: Murali Swaminathan is chief technology officer of Freshworks. He says AI is changing how software is built and how work gets done. Youngsters must use AI to delegate routine work so they can focus on solving more complex problems, he says.

Article Title: Spain turned a traffic roundabout into a public bath; the 6-day experiment was later named a climate refuge
Article Text:
Representative Image of a vibrant public bath in a traffic roundabout, complete with steam rooms and cold-water basins (AI Generated Image)

Round About Baths turned a traffic island into a temporary public bath

The climate reason behind a bath in a traffic roundabout

A temporary experiment in changing how cities use space

In Logroño, Spain, a traffic roundabout was temporarily transformed into a public bath, turning a space normally dominated by passing cars into a place for bathing and gathering. Called Round About Baths, the installation was designed by Leopold Banchini Architects for the 2025 edition of the Concéntrico architecture and design festival. Built around an existing fountain at the roundabout at Plaza Salón, on Gran Vía, the project added changing rooms, a steam room and cold-water basins behind timber walls. The installation operated from June 19 to 24, 2025, before the temporary structure was removed. Its unusual setting was part of the point: the project challenged the conventional role of road infrastructure by temporarily turning a car-dominated space into a place for people. The project's official European Prize for Urban Public Space profile also describes it as a temporary climate refuge for cases of extreme heat.The project began with the roundabout itself. According to Concéntrico's project description, the fountain at the centre was visible but inaccessible to pedestrians because of the surrounding traffic.The architects temporarily surrounded it with the facilities required for a public bath, creating an enclosed space inside an otherwise inaccessible part of the city. Leopold Banchini Architects designed the installation using a timber structure clad with uncut wooden panels. The arrangement included changing rooms, a steam room and cold-water basins, creating a sequence that moved visitors from the heated interior space to the outdoor area where they could cool down.The project was not simply an installation to be viewed from outside. For the period in which it operated, it functioned as a public bathing facility. According to the official user guide, sessions lasted 45 minutes, capacity was limited, and visitors entered in timed slots. Participants were required to bring their own towel and wear a bathing suit. The experience began in the hot steam room before continuing outdoors, where visitors could rest and cool down in the cold-water basins. The installation also had rules intended to preserve privacy and make the unusual setting workable. Changing areas were positioned on either side of the entrance, while personal belongings were placed in individual bags and held by staff during each session. Children under five were not permitted to enter, and users were asked to maintain silence, respect and considerate behaviour.The project's climate dimension becomes clearer in its later recognition by the European Prize for Urban Public Space. The prize's official project description calls Round About Baths a temporary public bath and “climate refuge” for cases of extreme heat, saying that it challenges the meaning of road infrastructure by turning space intended for vehicles into a place where people can meet at a human scale. That framing does not mean the installation was presented as a permanent solution to extreme heat. It was an ephemeral architectural project that operated for only a few days. Instead, its climate function was tied to the way water and bathing could temporarily change how people experienced an urban space during periods of heat.The design also made use of an existing piece of infrastructure rather than requiring an entirely new site. The fountain, which had previously been visible but inaccessible, became part of a functioning public bath. High timber walls provided privacy from the surrounding traffic, while the steam room and cold-water basins created spaces for heating and cooling within the temporary structure. The festival's own description also emphasises the project's broader urban argument. It says the installation revealed the hidden potential of a car-dominated environment by temporarily repurposing street equipment and changing how people perceived a forgotten space.Round About Baths was designed to be reversible. The tall walls were made from a regular timber structure and uncut wooden panels that were intended to have a second life after the festival. Once the temporary installation was removed, the fountain could return to its previous state. That reversibility was important to the project's architectural approach. Instead of permanently rebuilding a traffic junction, the intervention temporarily tested a completely different use for it. A space normally experienced from inside a passing car became a destination where people could stop, change clothes, enter a steam room and cool themselves in water.The project was subsequently selected as one of the five finalists for the 2026 European Prize for Urban Public Space, which recognises projects that create, recover or transform public space in European cities. The official prize profile places Round About Baths among projects exploring how urban infrastructure can be reconsidered for human and environmental needs. For several days in June 2025, therefore, the centre of a Spanish traffic roundabout was no longer simply something drivers passed around. It became a functioning public bath and, in the framing of the European Prize for Urban Public Space, a temporary refuge from extreme heat. The experiment was short-lived, but its central question was broader: whether infrastructure built primarily for cars can also be adapted, even temporarily, to provide spaces for people, water, cooling and communal life.
Article Summary: The installation was designed by Leopold Banchini Architects for the 2025 edition of the Concéntrico architecture and design festival. Built around an existing fountain, the project added changing rooms, a steam room and cold-water basins behind timber walls. The installation operated from June 19 to 24, 2025, before the temporary structure was removed.

Article Title: In 2002, Houston built a runway for Boeing 747s using a concrete mix with 25% fly ash and 25% blast-furnace slag; test slabs reached 800 psi flexural strength in 90 days
Article Text:
AI-generated representative image showing the reconstruction of Houston’s George Bush Intercontinental Airport runway with a high-performance concrete pavement designed for heavy aircraft. Credits - Gemini

Houston required a new runway

The ternary mix explained

The caution from Houston's other runway

AI-generated representative image showing a concrete flexural-strength test used to evaluate pavement material similar to the mix developed for Houston’s heavy-duty airport runway. Credits - Gemini

What the results show

Runway concrete must do more than hold up aircraft. It must hold up to repeated heavy loads, resist moisture and be structurally sound for years, which makes the choice of cementitious materials very critical. Engineers at Houston’s George Bush Intercontinental Airport sought to meet those criteria while substituting half of the traditional cement with industrial by-products. Runway 15R-33L opened to air traffic on June 13, 2002. The runway was 10,000 feet long and 150 feet wide, designed to take Boeing 747s, Antonov 124s and other big aircraft. Its most remarkable feature, however, was hidden in the concrete: half of the cementitious material was composed of 25% Class F fly ash and 25% blast-furnace slag.In a 2003 Concrete International article , Shondeep L. Sarkar and Adil Godiwalla described the material properties and early performance of the runway concrete. After about eight months of service, they reported high strength, low permeability and a dense concrete structure.The original Runway 15R-33L was not intended for the size of the aircraft Houston expected. It was just 6,038 feet long and 100 feet broad. There was approximately 15 inches of full-depth asphalt over six inches of lime- stabilised subgrade.It was originally designed based on a DC-9 weighing roughly 121,000 pounds. The renovation extended it to 10,000 feet and widened it to 150 feet, allowing the runway to accommodate Boeing 747-class aircraft with maximum weights of around 875,000 pounds. The $100 million job, regarded as the largest runway whitetopping project at a U.S. airport at the time, was covered in a comprehensive ASCE project paper on the rebuilding of Runway 15R-33L.Whitetopping involves placing a new concrete pavement over an existing pavement structure rather than removing the entire roadway. For the runway upgrade, engineers milled about 8 inches of asphalt in the keel section before placing a 19-inch concrete overlay, allowing the existing pavement structure to remain part of the rebuilt runway. The finished concrete road was about 18 inches thick and covered some 300,000 square yards. It had to be designed to withstand bending forces generated by very large aeroplanes moving across the slab time and again.A ternary blend is a mixture of three cementitious materials. The concrete at Bush Intercontinental had 50% Type I portland cement, 25% Class F fly ash and 25% Grade 120 blast-furnace slag by mass of the cementitious material. Fly ash is fine waste from the combustion of coal and blast-furnace slag is a by-product of iron manufacture. Both can participate in chemical reactions within the concrete and contribute to later age strength and a denser internal structure.The pavement was developed by the engineers of Houston for a flexural strength of 650 pounds per square inch. Trial batches were above the design target, reaching 800 psi in flexure at 90 days. Flexural strength is of special concern for pavements, since concrete slabs flex under the passage of aeroplane loads. A pavement mixture can therefore be evaluated not only by the compressive force it can withstand but also by its resistance to bending and cracking under repeated aircraft loads.The early field results were encouraging. The 2003 study found compressive strengths of roughly 6,730 to 9,790 psi in cores sampled after about eight months of service. Electrical testing indicated low permeability, while microscopic analysis found a dense concrete structure with little microcracking.Not every batch of concrete acted the same in Houston. Engineers later explored trouble at a critical runway intersection at neighbouring William P. Hobby Airport, which used a high-early-strength concrete mixture. ASCE performed a different study on the Hobby Airport runway restoration, indicating the service life of the previous pavement was decreased and the deterioration was mostly caused by the production of secondary ettringite crystals. Given the great emphasis on minimising runway closure time, fast strength development was a crucial feature of the original design.That experience did not suggest that high early-strength concrete was intrinsically unfit. It demonstrated that a pavement mix must be tailored to project conditions and priorities. Maximising early strength solves one problem of building but raises other problems of durability. Bush Intercontinental Runway went a different route. The ternary concrete was meant to develop significant strength at later ages while also offering low permeability. The fly ash and slag lowered the percentage of ordinary portland cement while maintaining the ability of the concrete to meet the structural requirements of the runway.There were tradeoffs. Cementitious blends with high proportions of fly ash and slag produce strength differently than plain portland-cement mixes; therefore, curing, building and opening needs need to be considered in design. A runway closure to allow concrete to gain strength presents a different problem than an emergency repair that must be opened within hours.Houston’s Runway 15R-33L demonstrated at full scale that a heavy-duty airport pavement could use a cementitious blend containing 50% industrial by-products. Trial concrete achieved 800 psi flexural strength at 90 days vs. a design basis of 650 psi. Initial field cores indicated satisfactory compressive strength and minimal permeability. It was not just a case of replacing Portland cement with waste materials. Engineers had to find a blend that was right for the aircraft loads, the construction process and the long-term durability needs.Houston’s experience at Hobby Airport offers a contrasting lesson: concrete designed for very rapid strength gain still needs to be evaluated for long-term durability. At Bush Intercontinental, the engineers instead used substantial amounts of fly ash and slag and designed the mix around the aircraft loads, construction requirements and expected service conditions.
Article Summary: Runway 15R-33L opened to air traffic on June 13, 2002. It was 10,000 feet long and 150 feet wide, designed to take Boeing 747s, Antonov 124s and other big aircraft. Half of the cementitious material was composed of 25% Class F fly ash and 25% blast-furnace slag.

Article Title: PewDiePie’s OpenAI controversy takes a new turn with his “less restricted” Ajax AI
Article Text:
PewDiePie (Image via Getty)

PewDiePie’s Ajax AI model focuses on local, private computing

PewDiePie’s OpenAI controversy adds another layer to Ajax

PewDiePie is stepping into the AI race with a project that is less about building the biggest model and more about making AI personal. Felix Kjellberg has introduced Ajax, a compact language model designed to run locally through his self-hosted Odysseus workspace. The project has also drawn attention because Kjellberg says OpenAI suspended his account twice during development, with one displayed email citing “distillation.” Ajax is built on Alibaba’s Qwen3.5-9B and aims to handle everyday tasks while keeping processing closer to the user’s own hardware.Ajax takes a different path from the giant cloud-based models dominating the AI industry. Its foundation, Qwen3.5-9B, has around nine billion parameters, making it far smaller than many frontier systems.That size is part of the appeal. Kjellberg is designing Ajax for practical jobs such as web searches, browsing, emails and calendars rather than trying to compete on every possible AI benchmark.The model is intended to operate as an “always-on” assistant inside Odysseus. A local setup could give users more control over their data and reduce the need to send routine requests to an external server.However, Ajax is still far from a finished consumer product.The project had not published final hardware requirements, independent benchmark results or downloadable model weights when the announcement was made. Its website was still listing the model as “Coming soon.”The most unusual part of the project involves how Kjellberg says he developed Ajax. He wanted to use outputs from a larger AI system to help create training material for his smaller model, a process known as knowledge distillation.OpenAI allows distillation in some contexts, but its terms restrict using its output to develop competing models and prohibit certain forms of automated extraction. Kjellberg says his account was suspended twice while working on Ajax. One email he displayed reportedly cited “distillation” as the reason.OpenAI has not publicly provided a specific explanation for those account actions, so Kjellberg’s account remains the main source for those details.Ajax is also designed to behave differently from many mainstream assistants. Its creators describe its refusal behaviour as having been “ablated” to create a freer system. Kjellberg reportedly used the open-source Heretic tool for this process.Still, the project retains limits around harmful requests. Its safety claims have not undergone an independent assessment, so they should not be treated as proof that Ajax is safe.Kjellberg plans more reinforcement learning, quantisation and benchmarking before a later release. For now, Ajax represents something broader than a celebrity-built chatbot. It reflects a growing interest in smaller AI models that can run locally, offer greater control and reduce dependence on powerful cloud platforms.

Article Title: In 1987, Delaware built Interstate 495 access ramps with nearly 10,000 tons of stockpiled fly ash; two years later, settlement was under one-eighth of an inch, matching conventional fill
Article Text:
I-495 northbound at the 12th Street interchange in Wilmington | Wikimedia Commons

Coal ash beneath a highway ramp

Engineers monitored the site

I-495 southbound approaching interchange with US 13 and DE 3 in Edgemoor | Wikimedia Commons

Part of a wider highway experiment

Delaware highway engineers used nearly 10,000 tons of stockpiled fly ash to construct two access ramps for an Interstate 495 interchange near Wilmington in June 1987. The material was supplied by Delmarva Power and Light Company's Edge Moor power plant. Engineers had to monitor the site for two years to measure settlement and check groundwater and other environmental conditions.The project used approximately 8,300 cubic yards of landfilled fly ash, which was placed in 12-inch loose layers and compacted with a smooth-drum vibratory roller. The completed embankment ranged from 4 to 16 feet deep along a section about 450 feet long. A Transportation Research Board report that documented the project says that the fly ash met or exceeded Delaware Department of Transportation compaction requirements. The material was used for two interchange ramps that connected I-495 with Edgemoor Road in Wilmington.Fly ash is a fine material that is produced by coal combustion, and for decades, large quantities accumulated at power plants, which created a disposal problem and prompted highway agencies to examine construction uses for the material. The Delaware project was one of several highway applications of fly ash recorded by the Federal Highway Administration, and its database lists the 1987 I-495 project in Wilmington at 6,300 cubic meters, or about 8,300 cubic yards.The EPA report says that engineers installed four groundwater monitoring wells and four permeate collection drains, while also collecting and analysing runoff and leachate from the area around the ash fill. Settlement was measured at designated settlement plates during the monitoring period, and the EPA reported less than one-eighth of an inch of settlement at each location. Its assessment also found no significant environmental effects during the two-year monitoring period.The report compared the in-place soil characteristics with those of well-compacted granular soil, and the measurements gave engineers information about how the fly ash behaved after being placed beneath the highway ramps. Engineers also monitored groundwater conditions around the fill and examined whether material from the ash moved into nearby soil or water. The findings provided additional data on the long-term performance of the highway embankment and the conditions that surrounded the construction site.Federal highway records now list more than 20 fly ash embankment or structural-backfill projects across the United States, with the projects including highway ramps, road embankments, and other transportation structures. The Federal Highway Administration's records list two Delaware projects, one being the 1987 I-495 work in Wilmington and the second being a 1992 Route 1 project in Dover. The agency estimated the Wilmington project at 6,300 cubic meters of material.Fly ash could be used in large quantities as embankment material because it did not have to become part of the finished road surface, and engineers could place it beneath the roadway while monitoring its physical performance and environmental conditions. The Wilmington project also became part of federal documentation on the use of coal fly ash in highway construction, and the recorded results included limited settlement during monitoring and no significant environmental effects during the period covered by the EPA study. The ramps that were built in 1987 were therefore more than a conventional road construction project. Beneath part of the I-495 interchange near Wilmington was a large quantity of material that had previously been stored as a coal-combustion byproduct.
Article Summary: Fly ash is a fine material that is produced by coal combustion. Large quantities accumulated at power plants, which created a disposal problem and prompted highway agencies to examine construction uses for the material. Engineers had to monitor the site for two years to measure settlement and check groundwater and other environmental conditions.

Article Title: In 1987, Mississippi rebuilt 1.5 miles of State Route 15 with pond ash from a coal plant; after three years, its stronger ash sections bent far less than the ordinary control road
Article Text:
From coal ash to road construction | Wikimedia Commons

Five test sections on one road

Engineers measured how the road moved

Illustration of water pollution wastewater streams at typical coal-fired electric power plants in the United States | Wikimedia Commons

Three years of field data

Mississippi rebuilt about 1.5 miles of State Route 15 in Stone County in 1987 by using pond ash from subbituminous coal. The project divided the roadway into five test sections, with four using lime-stabilized ash and one using cement-stabilized ash, while a separate 0.85-mile section used mechanically stabilized sand-clay material as the control. Engineers used the sections to compare the performance of different ash mixtures with the control section, and the road was monitored after construction, with measurements taken over the following three years to assess pavement condition and deflection.Pond ash is a mixture of ash materials collected and stored in settling ponds at coal-fired power plants, and the project was designed to examine pond ash as a base material for a paved road. The five test sections used different stabilization mixes, with four containing lime at concentrations that ranged from 2% to 7%, and one using 7.5% Portland cement. The control section used mechanically stabilized sand-clay subbase material.All of the sections were mixed in place, and a double bituminous surface treatment was then applied as the road's wearing surface. The Federal Highway Administration recorded the project in its User Guidelines for Waste and Byproduct Materials in Pavement Construction , and lists the Mississippi project as an example of a stabilized road base using Class C pond ash.The roadway was monitored after construction, and deflection measurements were taken every year through 1990. Deflection is the amount a pavement surface moves under a load, and engineers use the measurement to assess how a pavement responds when traffic places a load on it. The FHWA record says that the sections that contained 6% and 7% lime, along with the 7.5% cement section, recorded much lower deflection readings than the control section and the section containing only 2% lime.It did not mean that every ash mixture performed identically, since the type and amount of stabilizing material mattered. The control section and the 2% lime section had no observed cracking after three years, while the cement-stabilized section had the most cracking. The FHWA classified the cracking as shrinkage-related rather than structural, and noted that shrinkage cracking is common in cement-stabilized granular materials, particularly soil-cement mixtures.A separate Federal Highway Administration record of the Mississippi project describes the work as an evaluation of power plant pond ash for highway construction. The study tracked the test sections for three years and included measurements of pavement deflection, visible distress, ride quality, and the strength of material cores. The project report says that both the test sections and the control section provided good performance during the three-year service period.The results provided highway engineers with field data on several different ash mixtures rather than a single yes-or-no test. The control section provided a conventional comparison, while the stabilized ash sections showed how changes in lime and cement content affected pavement behavior. The FHWA's later guidance lists the Mississippi project among documented applications of coal ash in stabilized road bases.The Route 15 project was built as a field test, but the road was still a working state highway, and by 1990, engineers had three years of measurements from sections built with pond ash and from the conventional control section. The records show lower deflection in the stronger stabilized ash sections, while the observed cracking remained nonstructural, and the project became one of the documented U.S. examples of coal combustion material being used in highway pavement construction.
Article Summary: Mississippi rebuilt about 1.5 miles of State Route 15 in Stone County in 1987 by using pond ash from subbituminous coal. Five test sections used different stabilization mixes, with four containing lime at concentrations that ranged from 2% to 7%. The control section used mechanically stabilized sand-clay subbase material.

Article Title: A North Dakota farm kid turned ag-tech entrepreneur; his company puts real farm maps on children's play rugs
Article Text:
Representative Image of a colorful map-themed play rug featuring various agricultural fields and farm buildings (AI Generated Image)

From a North Dakota farm to agricultural mapping

How the play-rug idea began

What Boundri sells today

The " carpet farming " idea

A North Dakota farm kid has turned real agricultural maps into children's play rugs, giving toy tractors and combines a miniature version of the landscapes they come from. Nathan Faleide, founder of Boundri, grew up on a farm in North Dakota and around agricultural mapping through his family's Satshot business. Boundri was started in 2022 and grew from a play rug Faleide made for his children into a company that now puts personalised maps on rugs and other products. Today, Boundri sells mapped play rugs, blankets, wall maps, prints and other customised products, while its mapping background stretches back decades through the Faleide family's work in agricultural technology.Faleide's connection to farming began early. On Boundri's current About Us page, he says he grew up on a farm in North Dakota and that farm toys were central to his daily routine. He also says he "did farm a little" himself, but adds that it "wasn't my time." At the same time, he grew up around agricultural mapping through his family's company, Satshot. Faleide says that experience helped develop his expertise in software and maps, eventually providing the technical background behind Boundri.Satshot's history dates to 1994, when Lanny Faleide, Nathan's father, built software to create variable-rate maps using satellite imagery.Satshot says Lanny had more than 20 years of farming experience at the time and that the idea grew from flying as a pilot over his own fields and those of neighbouring farmers in the mid-to-late 1980s. The company also links the development of the technology to difficult conditions in farming during that period. The technology has since continued under Boundri. Satshot's current website describes Satshot as a brand, service and product of Boundri Inc., and says the technology created by Lanny has continued in a new direction with Nathan Faleide. It also says Boundri will continue to run the Satshot brand, product and service "for the time being" while developing new connections and tools around mapping and imagery.The first idea was much closer to home. On Boundri's own website, Faleide says the business began with a farm-toy play rug he made for his children. He describes the family as the inspiration for Boundri and says the project grew after seeing the enjoyment his children got from the rug. DTN reported in December 2022 that Faleide had nearly 25 years of experience in precision agriculture and mapping at the time and had long wanted to do more imagery-based art. The publication reported that when he introduced an early prototype, his children began playing with their farm toys on it. A photograph of the rug was subsequently shared by a friend on Twitter, after which orders began arriving. DTN reported that about 230 orders came in while the business was still in its early stages.AgWeb also reported that the product gained attention on Twitter as the business began taking off. An autumn 2022 report from Agweek described Boundri's initial offering as generic farm-print rugs, with custom products expected to follow. The early launch eventually developed into the personalised products that now form a major part of Boundri's range. Rather than limiting the designs to generic farm scenes, the company built its products around maps and imagery connected to specific locations.Farm play rugs remain one of Boundri's main products. Its current site lists personalised farm play rugs in three sizes and also offers custom-upload rugs and other mapped products. The company says its rugs are made from polyester chenille, have hemmed edges and a no-skid polyester backing, and can be cleaned with dish soap, a rag and a hose. It also says the rugs fold for storage and are lightweight. For customers who already have their own imagery, Boundri's FAQ provides more specific instructions. It says satellite, plane or drone images can be uploaded through the company's Custom Product Builder, rather than through its main-page products. The FAQ says the files must currently be JPG or PNG and smaller than 50 MB.Boundri's product page also explains the proof process. Customers can order an item and then send a note explaining any changes they want. The company says a proof is provided before the item is printed. The business now extends beyond children's play rugs. Boundri's website lists blankets, puzzles, onesies, canvas prints and other mapped products, while its wall-map and mural work can include features such as field boundaries, attributes and other map layers. The company says these custom projects are handled on a case-by-case basis.The phrase "carpet farming" appears in both coverage of Boundri and the company's own current website. DTN used the phrase when it covered the business in 2022, while Boundri uses it on its product pages to describe the children who play with its farm rugs. Its current Custom Upload Rugs page, for example, describes the product as a gift for "little carpet farmers."The concept gives children something more specific than a generic farm-themed play surface. Boundri's products can represent actual locations, turning maps associated with farms and other meaningful places into physical objects that can be used, displayed or given as gifts. For Faleide, the business brings together two parts of his background: farming and agricultural mapping. The technology behind Satshot grew from his family's experience with agricultural imagery and mapping, while Boundri has taken that knowledge into a very different kind of product. What began with a farm-toy rug for his own children has grown into a business built around putting maps onto objects people can use and keep.
Article Summary: Nathan Faleide grew up on a farm in North Dakota and around agricultural mapping through his family's company, Satshot. The company's history dates to 1994, when Lanny Faleid built software to create variable-rate maps using satellite imagery. Today, Boundri sells mapped play rugs, blankets, wall maps and other customised products.

Article Title: ‘Time for trial and error is over’: OpenAI safety employee David Robinson quits over AI risks
Article Text:
David Robinson made the comments in an article titled "I Quit OpenAI Because Its Culture Is Broken".

A former OpenAI safety employee has resigned from the company, warning that its rapid development of increasingly capable AI systems could raise the risk of serious failures. David Robinson said the “time for trial and error is over” and argued that AI companies need to put far greater emphasis on safety before developing more powerful systems.Robinson made the comments in an article titled "I Quit OpenAI Because Its Culture Is Broken", published by The Atlantic on Saturday.Robinson said AI companies, including OpenAI, were not being "nearly careful enough" and argued that safety research and expertise should play a much bigger role before more powerful AI systems are developed.Robinson spent 3-1/2 years at OpenAI, where he helped draft the company's preparedness framework and oversaw safety reports for 12 frontier-model launches. He said the company's focus on moving quickly from one AI model launch to another was making it difficult to maintain the level of caution he believed was necessary."As the company sprints from one launch to the next, it is failing to achieve the level of care that I believe is needed."He argued that the development of advanced AI should no longer rely on a process of repeatedly releasing systems, finding problems and fixing them afterwards.OpenAI refers to this approach as "iterative deployment", under which systems are released and their safeguards are strengthened as new problems are identified.Robinson argued that this approach is no longer sufficient as AI systems become more powerful."The time for trial and error is over," he wrote, saying advanced AI systems should have safeguards comparable to those used in high-risk fields such as nuclear power and aviation.His criticism comes amid a wider debate in the AI industry over whether companies are developing increasingly powerful systems faster than their ability to understand and control them. OpenAI and rival Anthropic have both faced scrutiny following incidents involving failed safety controls or unexpected behaviour from experimental AI systems.Robinson also warned that AI capabilities are advancing faster than researchers' understanding of alignment. AI alignment refers to efforts to ensure that AI systems behave in ways that are consistent with human goals and values.OpenAI defended its approach, saying it continues to put safety measures in place and can slow development when necessary."We're making sure our models don't become more capable than we can safely manage and secure, and we pause training or hold back models when we need to slow down," an OpenAI spokesperson said in a statement.
Article Summary: David Robinson said the “time for trial and error is over” and argued that AI companies need to put far greater emphasis on safety. Robinson spent 3-1/2 years at OpenAI, where he helped draft the company's preparedness framework and oversaw safety reports for 12 frontier-model launches.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.

Article Title: In 2023, a London house-clearance crew found two old computers buried under boxes; they were two of only three known surviving Q1 microcomputers, and the 1972 model later sold for £37,179
Article Text:
In 2023, a London house-clearance crew found two old computers buried under boxes; they were two of only three known surviving Q1 microcomputers, and the 1972 model later sold for £37,179/Image: Heritage Auctions via SWNS​

Computers that predated the Apple 1

Rare machines went on public display

First auction made value uncertain

The world's first fully integrated desktop computer was found among boxes during a London house clearance in 2023, with one of the rare machines later sold for £37,179 at auction. The computers were discovered by house-clearance firm Just Clear while workers were clearing a London property. The find included a 1972 Q1 desktop microcomputer with an internal printer and its slightly later sibling, the Q1 Lite.Only three Q1 microcomputers are known to have survived, which makes the two machines particularly rare. A companion printer designed for the Q1 Lite was also found during the clearance. The three devices were later offered for the first time at auction by Dallas-based Heritage Auctions. The 1972 Q1 achieved the highest price, selling for £37,179. The Q1 Lite sold for £8,316, while its companion printer fetched £1,175.All three machines were sold without a reserve.The Q1 dates back to 1972, four years before Steve Wozniak and Steve Jobs introduced the Apple 1.The machine used a microprocessor-based architecture that allowed it to deliver capabilities that had previously been associated with much larger computer systems.Valarie Spiegel, Heritage Auctions' director of video games, said the technology allowed the Q1 to “punch well above its weight” and established an important precedent for the computing industry.The Q1 was also far from affordable by the standards of the time. The machines would have cost the equivalent of more than £70,000 each, making them too expensive to be marketed for individual use.Despite that limitation, the Q1 represented an early step towards the development of computers that could eventually become part of everyday life.The computers did not go directly from the London house clearance to the auction block.The Q1, Q1 Lite and companion printer were displayed at Kingston University in London in February 2024, as part of an exhibition titled Creating the Everything Device: Showcasing the Machines That Built the Future.The exhibition focused on early computers and gaming machines and placed the newly discovered Q1s alongside other examples of early technology.Paul Neve, a senior lecturer at Kingston University, said having two Q1 machines available for the exhibition offered an opportunity to show the technology that preceded modern computers.“It is a real bonus being able to feature two Q1s, the world’s earliest microcomputers, at Kingston University,” Neve told New Atlas.He said the computers developed during the 1970s and 1980s helped establish the foundations for modern machines used for work, communication, productivity and entertainment.The Heritage sale was also significant because the machines had never previously been auctioned.Before the bidding began, Sara Balbi, managing director of Heritage Auctions' London office, said there was no established auction record for the Q1s that could indicate how much buyers might pay.“Keep in mind these have never been to auction, and there is no record or precedent set for them. We'll have to see what the market decides,” Balbi said.The eventual results put a value on the rare pieces of computing history.The 1972 Q1 with its internal printer sold for £37,179, while the later Q1 Lite reached £8,316. The separate Q1 companion printer sold for £1,175.
Article Summary: The Q1 was the world's first fully integrated desktop computer. It was found among boxes during a London house clearance in 2023. The 1972 model later sold for £37,179, while the later Q1 Lite reached £8,316. The separate Q1 companion printer fetched £1,175.

Article Title: Google pauses open-source bug bounty program after rise in AI spam submissions
Article Text:
What changes and what stays active

Read Google VRP’s post

PSA for open-source bug hunters

We are temporarily no longer accepting OSS VRP product vulnerability submissions.

This does not impact OSS VRP supply chain reports, or any outstanding reports. As an alternative, we encourage you to find impact across our other VRP programs and submit there instead, or pursue the Patch Rewards Program.

Why is this happening? This pause is due to a significant rise in automated submissions, the vast majority of which are not valid. We will continue to reformat and work on this aspect of the OSS VRP and commit to giving an update in Q1 2027.

Google has paused product vulnerability submissions for its Open Source Software Vulnerability Reward Program (OSS VRP) after a flood of invalid, AI-generated reports overwhelmed security engineers and repository maintainers. The company announced the operational freeze in a post on X, directing security researchers toward its other active reward initiatives. Google stated that it will use the downtime to restructure the submission framework, with an official progress update slated for the first quarter of 2027.The suspension took effect immediately on October 1, though Google outlined specific exceptions to avoid shutting down critical disclosure channels. One of them is that the pause does not affect valid product vulnerability filings logged before October 1. The freeze applies specifically to product vulnerability reports; supply chain disclosures submitted under the OSS VRP remain open.Certain product vulnerability reports tied to Google Cloud repositories that directly impact Cloud products may still be accepted through the separate Google Cloud VRP.Previously, Linux maintainers reported being completely flooded by bogus Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) filings after automated AI hunters drove recorded vulnerabilities to a record high of 2,000 per release. The influx forced the Linux project to drop support for older network drivers.Chipmaker Intel also recently froze its bug bounty program, which offered payouts reaching $100,000 per flaw. While Intel did not cite synthetic submissions as the official cause, industry analysts widely attribute the shutdown to identical AI spam bottlenecks.
Article Summary: Google has paused product vulnerability submissions for its Open Source Software Vulnerability Reward Program. The company announced the operational freeze in a post on X, directing security researchers toward its other active reward initiatives. Google stated that it will use the downtime to restructure the submission framework, with a progress update slated for the first quarter of 2027.
