Article Title: ChatGPT for Teens: 5 features parents should know about, from homework help to screen time controls
Article Text:
Study Mode: guided learning instead of instant answers

Homework reminders that nudge teens away from shortcuts

Turning tough topics into quizzes and interactive visuals

Parental controls that set structure without constant monitoring

Smarter prompts can make revision genuinely more productive

As AI tools become a fixture in how teenagers study, OpenAI is positioning its ChatGPT for Teens offering as a way to support independent learning rather than simply hand over answers — pairing study-focused features with age-appropriate parental safeguards designed to address a common worry among parents: how to let teens use AI for homework without letting it do the work for them.At the center of ChatGPT for Teens is Study Mode, which turns a simple question into a more structured learning experience. Rather than jumping straight to a final answer, it breaks concepts down step by step, offers hints, asks follow-up questions, and checks a student's understanding along the way.Students are encouraged to use prompts like asking ChatGPT to show them where they went wrong, give a hint for the next step, or help them work through a problem without revealing the answer outright — shifting the interaction from "give me the answer" to "help me understand how to get there."To discourage teens from simply offloading assignments onto AI, ChatGPT includes homework reminders that kick in when it detects a teen may be trying to use the tool to complete an assignment outright. Instead of letting a prompt like "write my history assignment" go through as-is, the system is designed to redirect students toward exploring key arguments and building their response themselves, step by step, within Study Mode — framed as a gentle nudge toward using AI as a learning aid rather than a replacement for actual effort.For subjects that are hard to grasp through reading alone, teens can ask ChatGPT to convert a chapter into a quiz, generate practice questions, or explain a concept in a different way if the first explanation doesn't click. The platform also includes Learning Visualizations, which offer interactive ways to explore more than 70 core maths and science concepts — letting students actually see how formulas, graphs, and variables behave in real time, rather than relying purely on memorization.For parents, ChatGPT for Teens includes linked parental controls that don't require reading every conversation to maintain oversight. Parents can set Study Hours, during which new chats automatically open in Study Mode, and Quiet Hours, during which access to the app can be limited altogether.Beyond scheduling, parents can also manage specific features like voice mode and image generation, along with sensitive-content protections. In limited, high-risk situations involving serious self-harm concerns, the system is also designed to send parents a direct safety notification — a feature aimed at balancing a teen's need for independence with a parent's need to know when something serious may be happening.Beyond homework help, ChatGPT can also support structured exam revision. Teens are encouraged to ask it to quiz them on a chapter with increasingly difficult questions as they improve, build a 30-minute revision plan, test their recall by asking questions without access to their notes, or identify which areas need more review based on how they answered previous questions.Used this way, the tool is pitched less as a replacement for traditional studying and more as a way to make revision time more active and targeted, complementing — rather than substituting for — what students already learn from teachers and textbooks.
Article Summary: OpenAI's ChatGPT for Teens lets teens use AI to help them learn. Study Mode turns a simple question into a more structured learning experience. It offers hints, asks follow-up questions, and checks a student's understanding along the way.

Article Title: Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates says technology has truly stunned him only three times in his life, and the third happened this year when he looked closely at...
Article Text:
​Bill Gates, who wrote code before most of Silicon Valley was born, names the AI tool that stunned him this year

Bill Gates says coding is where AI's progress surprised him most

Gates expects AI to reshape software engineering jobs first

Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates says technology has truly stunned him only three times in his life, and the third came this year when he looked closely at Anthropic's AI coding tool, Claude Code. The first was in 1980, when he saw a graphical user interface for the first time, the idea that went on to shape the modern personal computer. The second was in 2022, when OpenAI 's leaders came to his house to demonstrate what would soon become ChatGPT.Claude Code hit differently because of what it does. Gates wrote code long before he became one of the world's richest people, and he calls it the subject he knows best. "The idea that now these things are in a meaningful sense better than I am is like: What the hell?" he said in a recent interview.Gates's reaction carries weight because of where he started. He began programming as a teenager in Seattle, and in 1975 he co-founded Microsoft with Paul Allen on the back of software they wrote themselves. For most of his life, writing good code was the skill that set him apart.He said that AI's recent improvements had far exceeded his expectations, and Claude Code was a big part of that shift. It was also one of the reasons he chose to speak out now.In a nearly 6,000-word essay published on his blog, Gates Notes, he warned that the transition to AI will be "one of the most turbulent times in human history," and that the world is not preparing for it.Claude Code is Anthropic's agentic coding tool. Developers can hand it programming tasks from the command line, desktop or mobile app, and it writes, edits and debugs code for them. Anthropic showcased it at its Code with Claude developer event in May.Gates has been tracking AI's impact on programmers for a while. Earlier this year, he wrote that AI already makes software developers at least twice as efficient, and that its rate of improvement was starting to disrupt job demand in software development.In his latest essay, he listed software engineering among the first fields likely to feel the effects, alongside sales, customer support and paralegal work. He did offer one caveat. As coding gets cheaper, demand for software could grow, so net job losses in the field may be smaller than elsewhere, as long as some tasks, such as design, are still better done by humans.Still, coming from someone who built a company on software, the admission stands out. The tool that shocked Gates this year did not beat him at something unfamiliar. It beat him at the thing he knows best.
Article Summary: Bill Gates says Claude Code, an AI coding tool, stunned him this year. He wrote code long before he became one of the world's richest people. "The idea that now these things are in a meaningful sense better than I am is like: What the hell?" he said.

Article Title: OpenAI fires three researchers, company confirms sacking; shares what investigations that led to termination revealed
Article Text:
OpenAI fires three researchers, company confirms sacking; shares what investigations that led to termination revealed

Alleged sharing of information with AI safety group

The connection to the Hugging Face breach

Part of a bigger reckoning inside OpenAI

A moment of mounting pressure on AI safety practices

ChatGPT-maker OpenAI has terminated three researchers from its safety team after an internal investigation concluded that they violated company policies governing access to and handling of sensitive information, according to a company statement and a Wall Street Journal report. The ChatGPT maker confirmed that the employees were dismissed following a probe into the handling of confidential company data. "We have parted ways with three individuals for violating our policies on accessing and handling sensitive company information," an OpenAI spokesperson said. "Our investigation confirmed that these individuals mishandled sensitive information outside established company procedures, violating our policies and breaking the trust essential to our work."According to a Wall Street Journal report, the three researchers are Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni, all of whom worked on safety and alignment-related efforts at the company.The report said the researchers were accused of sharing confidential company information with third-party AI safety organisations, including nonprofit research groups involved in evaluating advanced AI systems.One of the dismissed employees, Tomek Korbak, had publicly said he served as OpenAI's technical contact for AI safety organisations METR and Redwood Research during an investigation into a recent AI security incident involving OpenAI models.The other two researchers, Wang and Balesni, worked on AI alignment, a field focused on ensuring AI systems behave in accordance with human intentions and safety objectives. Neither of the affected employees immediately commented on the dismissals, according to the report.The firings are directly tied to OpenAI's response to a string of recent security incidents in which its AI agents escaped containment, including an incident in which one of its models hacked AI platform Hugging Face. In the aftermath of that breach, OpenAI allowed staff from AI safety nonprofit METR, along with a contracted staff member from Redwood Research, to work inside its offices for six days to investigate how its models had behaved. METR later published a report based on what it learned during that access.Korbak, one of the three fired researchers and a member of OpenAI's safety team, has said he served as the company's technical point of contact for Redwood Research and METR throughout their investigation into the Hugging Face incident. The other two terminated employees, Wang and Balesni, worked on alignment — the broader effort to ensure AI models behave in ways humans actually intend.The firings come as OpenAI works to investigate a range of agent security incidents uncovered in recent months and address the underlying safety issues behind them. Just this week, the company scrapped the planned launch of a new AI model, GPT-6.1 Astra, specifically over safety concerns, underscoring how seriously these incidents are being treated internally.In response to the broader wave of security failures, OpenAI says it has implemented a new monitoring system designed to catch AI-agent misbehavior more quickly, started requiring engineers to apply stronger security guardrails when testing its AI systems, and committed to sharing more information publicly when its models behave badly.The firings land at a moment when major AI labs are facing growing pressure to submit their technology for independent safety testing. Just last month, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said his company would allow outside evaluators like METR to verify its adherence to safety measures and assess model alignment — a step OpenAI had also taken, at least temporarily, in granting METR and Redwood Research access following the Hugging Face breach.That same climate of concern has produced other high-profile moments in recent weeks. In early September, Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon publicly resigned, saying he didn't want to be part of a rush to build AI systems capable of improving themselves, citing fears that such systems could spiral out of control and pose a threat to humanity. Around the same time, Amodei wrote publicly that the risks posed by today's most advanced AI tools were too significant to justify continuing development at the current breakneck pace, calling for an industry-wide slowdown — a call that drew public agreement from both OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Elon Musk.
Article Summary: OpenAI fires three researchers, company confirms sacking; shares what investigations that led to termination revealed. The researchers were accused of sharing confidential company information with third-party AI safety organisations. The firings are directly tied to OpenAI's response to a string of recent security incidents in which its AI agents escaped containment.

Article Title: Google ex-CEO Eric Schmidt: Best programmers don't write code anymore, they...
Article Text:
Eric Schmidt's idea of a top programmer goes to bed at 7 PM

The best programmers won't be replaced by AI—they'll become even more valuable

Schmidt says AI's real impact will be automating the 'boring' backbone of business

Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt says the most valuable programmers in the world have quietly redefined their job. They don't write code anymore. They write specifications, set evaluation criteria, hit run—and go to bed. It's a shift that Schmidt believes signals something much larger than a change in workflow—it's the beginning of AI reshaping how entire industries operate.Schmidt described a programmer at one of his startups who does exactly this. Every evening at 7 PM, he defines what he wants the AI to build, writes a test function to judge the output, and lets the system loose. Then he has dinner with his wife and goes to sleep. The AI churns through the night, finishing around 4 AM. By breakfast, the work is done. "This stuff would've taken me six months and 10 programmers at Google," Schmidt said. "This poor guy's sleeping."The natural assumption is that AI will make programmers obsolete. Schmidt thinks the opposite is true—at least for the elite ones. Top-tier engineers were always disproportionately valuable, worth roughly 10 times more than those just below them. That gap, he argued, is about to widen.The grunt work is disappearing, but the ability to orchestrate AI systems at scale—grasping parallelisation, defining the right constraints, judging when the output is good enough—is becoming the entire job.The real skill now isn't writing code, Schmidt suggested. It's framing the problem correctly and knowing what "good" looks like. "If you can define the evaluation function and you can let it run, and if you have enough hardware, you're inventing worlds," he said. AI systems at leading research labs are already handling a significant and growing share of programming work, making the engineers who direct them more critical, not less.Yet the bigger story, Schmidt argued, isn't about programmers at all. AI's largest economic payoff will come from automating the dull, expensive plumbing of corporate operations—billing, accounting, inventory management, delivery logistics—processes that silently drain billions from company budgets every year. "If anything, it's under-hyped because you are fundamentally automating businesses," he said at Harvard's John F. Kennedy Jr. Forum.He predicted artificial general intelligence could arrive as early as 2029, powered by recursive self-improvement—AI systems that learn and plan on their own, without waiting for human instruction. Schmidt also pointed to medicine, climate solutions, and engineering as fields where AI-driven automation could unlock breakthroughs that remain largely untapped today.
Article Summary: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt says the most valuable programmers in the world have quietly redefined their job. They don't write code anymore. They write specifications, set evaluation criteria, hit run and go to bed. Schmidt says AI's real impact will be automating the 'boring' backbone of business operations.

Article Title: Godfather of AI Yann LeCun does not believe that AI will kill humans; 'blames' humans for AI Agents hacking into companies' networks and government websites; says: “Those agents are doing exactly what
Article Text:
Godfather of AI Yann LeCun does not believe that AI will kill humans; 'blames' humans for AI Agents hacking into companies' networks and government websites; says: “Those agents are doing exactly what ...

Yann LeCun says AI risks are being exaggerated

Yann LeCun criticises AI safety warnings

Yann LeCun, widely known as the “godfather of AI”, does not believe artificial intelligence (AI) will wipe out humanity. Instead, LeCun says recent incidents in which AI agents hacked company networks and other systems were caused by poor human oversight and badly designed security systems. Speaking about the risks linked to AI agents, Yann LeCun said told Fortune: “Those agents are doing exactly what they’ve been asked to do,” adding that the systems were supposed to operate inside secure sandboxes. “They were supposed to be in sandboxes, but the sandboxes were leaky and horribly designed,” he said.Yann LeCun, who shared the 2018 Turing Award with Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio for their work on deep learning, said he has “zero concerns” about recent rogue AI incidents and is not worried “at all” about AI destroying humanity.He said incidents such as an OpenAI agent autonomously hacking Hugging Face could have been prevented through better system design and oversight. LeCun also argued that some AI labs do not have a strong enough understanding of cybersecurity. He said the risks from AI agents should be addressed through better safeguards rather than broad claims about AI becoming an existential threat.During the interaction, Yann LeCun has also criticised the growing focus on AI safety, particularly ideas linked to the effective altruism movement.He called the movement “super toxic” and a “complete disaster.”He also criticised warnings from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman that AI could pose serious risks to humanity. Amodei, LeCun said, is “honest”, but he accused him of supporting policies that could benefit large AI companies by making it harder for smaller competitors and open-source developers to compete.“Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman ‘saying, ‘AI can kill us all’ is incredibly destructive for everybody, including for the public who’s scared shitless,” LeCun said. He called such messaging “the worst marketing campaign you can possibly imagine.”
Article Summary: Yann LeCun does not believe that AI will kill humans. 'blames' humans for AI Agents hacking into companies' networks and government websites. “Those agents are doing exactly what they’ve been asked to do,” he said.

Article Title: Google Japan's Gboard Kurukuru keeps the keys moving so your fingers don't have to
Article Text:
Google's new keyboard brings the keys to you.

You can't buy Google's conveyor belt keyboard , but you can build one

Google Japan has a new keyboard out, and this time you don't go hunting for the keys because they come to you. The Gboard Kurukuru Version puts its keys on four little conveyor belts that keep rolling, and you simply tap the letter you want when it slides under your finger.There are 29 keys on each belt, so 116 in all. Capital and small letters get their own keys too, which means you never have to touch Shift.If you're worried about timing your taps, a voice calls out each key as it reaches a set point. Feeling confident? There's a speed mode that spins the belts faster. And if you miss your letter, well, you wait for it to come back around.It plays a lot like a rhythm game.The idea, Google says, is to make one-handed typing easier. On a normal keyboard your hand has to move around to find the keys, and that gets tiring fast with one hand, let alone one finger. Here the keys do the moving, so your other hand is free for the mouse or, as Google puts it, a cup of tea.The company even calls it a "Copernican revolution" in typing, and says you can build a second one if you want to type with both hands. "Kurukuru" loosely means spinning round and round in Japanese, which pretty much sums it up.As you'd expect, there's no buy option for this one. Google has instead put the whole design up on GitHub as an open-source project, so if you've got the parts and the patience, you can build one at home.This is the 15th keyboard Google Japan has dreamt up for October 1, a tradition that took over from its April Fools' jokes in 2021. The date is a little joke of its own, since 10/1 reads as 101, as in the old 101-key keyboard.Before this, we got the extra-long Gboard Bar, the wearable Gboard Caps and last year's Gboard Dial, which had you typing like you were dialling a rotary phone. Google says faster belts, longer and portable versions, and more colours could be next, so the wait for your next letter might get a bit shorter.
Article Summary: Gboard Kurukuru Version puts keys on four conveyor belts. You simply tap the letter you want when it slides under your finger. There are 29 keys on each belt, so 116 in all. Capital and small letters get their own keys too, so you never have to touch Shift.

Article Title: Microsoft AI launches MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming alongside multilingual MAI-Voice 2.1 models
Article Text:
Real-time speech recognition: MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming

Natural Multilingual Output: MAI-Voice-2.1

MAI-Voice-2.1-Flash Low-Latency Scale

Microsoft has launched MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming model, with Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman, calling it the most accurate real-time audio transcription model in the world. Unveiled alongside two companion speech generation models – MAI-Voice-2.1 and the high-speed MAI-Voice-2.1-Flash – the release is designed to provide developers with responsive, low-cost building blocks for building autonomous conversational voice agents.According to Suleyman, the new voice architecture delivers inference speeds that are 55% faster and operational costs that are 60% cheaper than comparable offerings like ElevenLabs. He said in a post on X (formerly Twitter): “We're launching the most accurate real time transcription model in the world... #1 !!! 55% faster and 60% cheaper than ElevenLabs. Come build agents on our platform!”The headline addition to the company’s audio lineup, MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming, provides continuous, low-latency live speech-to-text across 60 languages with built-in automatic language detection. Key performance benchmarks and features include top benchmark ranking as the model has secured the No. 1 spot for accuracy across both partial and completed transcripts on the independent benchmark platform Artificial Analysis.It sits on the Pareto frontier for accuracy versus latency, eliminating the historical tradeoff where high precision required sluggish processing times. Instead of pausing until a sentence ends, the model outputs initial text hypotheses within roughly 100 milliseconds of receiving incoming audio.It refines words as additional context arrives and finalizes stable text immediately.By surfacing partial transcripts as words are spoken, voice bots can trigger API tools and start logical reasoning before the user finishes speaking. For live captioning and automated dictation workflows, internal tests show text appears on-screen twice as fast as the nearest market competitor.To pair with speech recognition, the team introduced MAI-Voice-2.1, its flagship multilingual text-to-speech engine covering 23 languages and 26 regional locales.The system's standout capability is cross-lingual identity preservation. A single synthetic voice persona can switch seamlessly between diverse languages, such as English, Mandarin and German, without carrying a foreign accent over from one language to another. Instead, the synthesized speaker modifies actual local pronunciation and retains a unique vocal identity.That means brands can deploy uniform virtual ambassadors worldwide, educational sites can switch languages while keeping the same instructors, and customer support agents can respond in the caller’s language without missing a beat.MAI-Voice-2.1-Flash was introduced by the company for mission-critical, high-capacity applications that demand immediate response times.The Flash version offers the same 23-language voice consistency as the base model, but it is optimized for high-throughput enterprise workloads, and can produce 45 seconds of synthesized audio with an end-to-end latency of just 150 milliseconds.
Article Summary: MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming is the most accurate real-time audio transcription model in the world, says Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman. The release is designed to provide developers with responsive, low-cost building blocks for building conversational voice agents.

Article Title: Is Minecraft Dungeons 2 cross platform? Crossplay and multiplayer explained
Article Text:
Minecraft Dungeons II officially supports cross-platform (Image via Mojang)

Is Minecraft Dungeons 2 crossplay?

How co-op works in Minecraft Dungeons II

Turning on Cross-platform in Minecraft Dungeons II

Launch Minecraft Dungeons II and go to the main menu.

Open Settings and look for the Game options section.

Find Cross-Platform Play and toggle it on.

Crossplay vs. Cross-Progression

Subscription requirements

Minecraft Dungeons II launched on September 29, 2026, and the new dungeon crawler has received a solid reception from the community. For anyone planning to squad up with friends across different consoles, the good news arrived early: crossplay is fully supported.If you are looking for further details, you are at the right place. Here's a breakdown of how multiplayer works, what crossplay actually covers, and what to know before jumping into a session.Yes. Minecraft Dungeons II supports cross-platform play across every system it launched on: PC, Xbox, PlayStation, and Nintendo Switch, for parties of up to four players. This builds on a feature the original Minecraft Dungeons already had, so Mojang carried the functionality forward into the sequel rather than building it from scratch.Official store listings and Xbox have both confirmed cross-platform multiplayer and cross-platform co-op, meaning a group spread across PlayStation, Xbox, Switch, and PC can all land in the same session without workarounds. Mojang hasn't published a detailed platform-by-platform compatibility chart, so the exact mechanics of every possible pairing aren't fully spelled out.Minecraft Dungeons II supports up to four players at once, whether that's entirely online, entirely local couch co-op, or a mix of both happening in the same session.That hybrid option, officially called Mixed Co-Op, is one of the sequel's standout multiplayer additions, since the original game required players to choose one mode or the other rather than blending them.Joining a session works two ways: through matchmaking, which fills empty slots automatically, or by sharing an eight-character party code with friends so they can join a specific lobby directly, regardless of what platform they're on.Cross-platform play is tied to account sign-in rather than being fully automatic. To enable it:Once enabled, the setting stays active going forward unless manually turned off from the same menu.It's worth separating two related but different features. Crossplay lets players on different platforms share a session together. Cross-progression is about carrying a saved character from one platform to another. Mojang has confirmed that hero data is stored online rather than locally, so progress follows players who sign in with the same Microsoft account across devices.Online console multiplayer isn't entirely free of extra requirements. Xbox players need an active Game Pass tier that includes online multiplayer, while PlayStation players need an active PlayStation Plus subscription to play online. PC players don't need anything beyond owning the game, and it's also available through Game Pass on day one as an Xbox Play Anywhere title.To conclude it all, squads spread across different consoles can enjoy Minecraft Dungeons II together. Now you can easily jump into a friend's game using party codes and have a blast playing the game. The big things to double check before you go are having an active online subscription on consoles and making sure cross platform play is toggled on in settings.
Article Summary: Minecraft Dungeons II supports cross-platform multiplayer and co-op. This means a group spread across PlayStation, Xbox, Switch, and PC can all land in the same session without workarounds. Cross-progression is about carrying a saved character from one platform to another.

Article Title: From crash-test airbags to Formula E: Heron Preston’s journey with discarded materials
Article Text:
Heron Preston partners with Formula E to explore sustainable motorsport fashion

From sanitation uniforms to Formula E: Heron Preston gives waste a new life

Heron Preston brings crash-test airbags, recycled materials into Formula E fashion

From fashion to motorsport for Heron Preston

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For Heron Preston, discarded materials are not simply waste. They can become something new. The designer has built his work around finding new uses for materials that are often overlooked. Now, that approach is coming to motorsport through a creative partnership with Formula E, where fashion, performance and sustainability will come together. The partnership will explore how existing materials can be reused to create clothing, products and other items linked to motorsport.Heron Preston has explored the potential of unwanted materials through several projects. His 2016 UNIFORM project used upcycled decommissioned New York City Department of Sanitation uniforms and second-hand garments.More recently, he worked with Mercedes-Benz to transform crash-test airbags into garments. The clothes retained the distinctive physical qualities of the material. His approach is based on looking closely at every part of a product, from the materials used to how they are made and the people and processes involved. He calls this concept eX-Ray.ID@undefined Caption not available.Rather than simply choosing existing fabrics, eX-Ray looks at how materials can be developed and used in a more considered way.For the Formula E partnership, Heron Preston is using recycled cotton made from pre-consumer factory off-cuts and production scraps. The materials are sorted, shredded and re-spun into new yarn before being developed into a heavyweight, tightly woven fabric. The idea fits with Formula E’s own focus on recovering and reusing resources.While Preston turns recovered materials into new designs, Formula E uses regenerative braking to recover energy and use it again for racing. Together, the two sides want to explore how this thinking can be applied to motorsport fashion from the beginning of the design process.The partnership will look at more than clothing. The partners hope to explore performance wear, fan merchandise, accessories and products made from upcycled materials drawn from the sport. They also want to find new uses for components and materials after their life in racing.The GEN4 car provides an example of Formula E’s approach. It is designed to be 100% recyclable or reusable, with at least 20% recycled materials across key components.Talking about the same, Heron Preston said, “This creative partnership is about rethinking what motorsport fashion can be. I’ve always been interested in taking materials, processes and ideas from unexpected places and finding new ways to give them purpose. Working with Formula E gives me the opportunity to bring that approach into a world where performance is everything. We’re looking at how apparel can be thoughtfully designed from the material up, balancing function, quality and a more considered approach to how things are made.The partnership will be previewed at ComplexCon Los Angeles on October 3 and 4. The event will feature an exploration of eX-Ray materials and a GEN4 Formula E car with an exclusive Preston-designed livery.Ellie Norman, Chief Marketing Officer, Formula E, said, “Heron and Formula E share a curiosity about how things work and how they can be made better. In racing, we push for greater performance while using energy and materials more efficiently. Heron brings a complementary perspective, exploring what existing materials can become through design. This partnership gives us the opportunity to develop those ideas together and apply them to the products people wear. ComplexCon is the first look at that shared ambition, with the potential to build a more considered approach to motorsport fashion over time.”Also read: Formula E, Heron Preston join hands to bring recycled materials to motorsport fashion
Article Summary: Designer Heron Preston partners with Formula E to explore sustainable motorsport fashion. The partnership will explore how existing materials can be reused to create clothing, products and other items linked to motorsport. Preston has previously worked with Mercedes-Benz to transform crash-test airbags into garments.
